parameters.redaction_method: literal string substitution, verified against source text

stages.notes: Verified /app/assets/c4395d52.00.json exists and is a JSON array of 20 records with fields id, domain, policy, policy_ids, text.
Loaded and indexed all 20 records by id; read full policy text and body text for each to determine applicable redaction categories.

Applied literal (non-regex) string replacements per record via /app/redact.py, using a per-record entity-to-marker map so every occurrence/alias of the same entity received the same numbered marker. Verified exact substrings (including embedded newlines/whitespace) against source text before finalizing; re-ran with zero 'substring not found' warnings after fixes.

Manually reviewed all 20 redacted records line-by-line and scored each against the 5-criterion rubric. Overall average 4.73, minimum per-criterion average 4.60 (Context Preservation and Redaction Precision), both above thresholds.

One informal refinement round applied before formal scoring: fixed 4 missed/inconsistent redactions (record 1562 bare ID number, record 784 'sbwhoeop' alias, record 938 'Cdm' initials, record 16 unredacted persona names requiring segment-based disambiguation of two same-named personas). Formal scoring after these fixes passed on round 1; no further iteration rounds were required.
Wrote /app/results/summary.md with overview, rubric score table, per-record notes, iteration history, recommendations, and limitations.
Confirmed all 3 output files exist and are non-empty, and that redacted_dataset.json contains exactly 20 records each with a non-empty redacted_text field.
